newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, Ukraine agree Black Sea fleet deal -- Tass.
newsitem.headline: Russia, Ukraine agree Black Sea fleet deal -- Tass.

text.p: Russian leader Boris Yeltsin and Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma on Thursday resolved all problems surrounding the disputed Black Sea fleet, Itar-Tass news agency said.

It quoted Yeltsin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky as saying Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin would fly to Kiev in November to sign agreements on dividing up and financing the fleet. Several such deals have been announced in the past but the fate of the fleet has not yet been settled.
The dispute over the fleet has dragged on since the Soviet Union fell apart in late 1991 and has defied all previous attempts to solve it.

Just before the two leaders met, Russia's lower house of parliament warned Ukraine that Moscow would never hand over control of the Crimean port of Sevastopol, home to the fleet. But the parliamentary resolution had no legal force.

"The presidents reached agreement on all the questions. Before the middle of November it is expected that Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin will visit Kiev when a number of agreements will be signed on splitting up the fleet, where it will be based and on financing as well," Yastrzhembsky said.

Yeltsin promised Kuchma that his first official visit after he had recovered from heart surgery planned for next month would be to Kiev to sign a long-awaited agreement on relations betwen the two Slav states.
